  "type": "sector",

  "insights": [
   "European bank earnings expectations for FY2026 have been revised up +28% since 1 Feb 2024, the largest among Stoxx sectors, ahead of Energy +25% and Utilities +12%.",
   "The bank recovery story is shifting from sector re-rating to an earnings and capital returns story, so selectivity matters more than owning the sector as a whole.",
   "European bank earnings only regained 2007 levels in 2023, and analysts expect further increases in coming years.",
   "European bank ROE has recovered to about 14%, near pre-financial-crisis levels, versus 4-7% in the low-rate era when banks traded below book and failed to cover cost of capital.",
   "The rally does not mean the opportunity is exhausted, since higher profitability supports higher valuations and future returns come more from earnings growth and capital returns.",
   "Balance sheet reinvestment is a multi-year tailwind: low-yielding long-term investments are maturing and being reinvested at higher yields, especially for banks in Italy, Spain, Greece and Portugal.",
   "Southern European banks benefit from deposit margins lasting longer, as lending rates repriced quickly while deposit rates rose slowly.",
   "Capital allocation matters more: large capital bases can fund dividends, buybacks, organic growth, technology and M&A. JPMorgan posted Q3 2026 net income of USD 15.3 billion as an example.",
   "Regional earnings drivers diverge across Europe, the US and Asia, including rate cycles, loan growth, deposit competition, wealth management, payments and capital markets.",

  "source": "Allianz Research",
  "title": "Crossing the Duration Desert: Who will buy and who will supply the long end of the curve?",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-25",
  "insights": [
   "Global gross duration supply peaked in 2021 at about USD6.5tn in 10-year equivalents. It is USD6.5tn in 2025 and USD5.6tn year-to-date, still elevated but slowing for all main issuers except China.",
   "Net duration supply after buybacks and roll-down fell from USD3.3tn in 2021 to USD2.1tn in 2025. About USD1tn in 2026 would be the lowest since 2018.",
   "The UK, Japan and the euro area add no new duration in 2026. The US and China each provide about half of net supply, and China's share is growing and should surpass the US. China's market is largely closed to global investors, so accessible duration is shrinking.",
   "Sovereigns have shortened issuance duration by 1 to 3 years since the 2022 rate shock. Weighted issuance duration fell from 7 to 6 years in the US and from 11 to 8 years in the euro area, while China rose from 5 to 7 years.",
   "Convenience yield has been under pressure since 2022 and is negative for the US, UK, France and Japan. Germany's remains positive. This favors more bills and fewer bonds, and the US 'Active Treasury Issuance' policy includes long-end buybacks of USD94bn in 2026.",
   "Hedge funds are now dominant marginal buyers of duration, holding about USD6tn of sovereign exposure funded in repo. About 60% of the rise in US positions is linked to basis trades. Pensions and central banks are stepping back.",
   "Hedge fund demand is leveraged, price sensitive and volatile. It adds a collateral and funding layer to monetary policy transmission, so central banks will favor reversible tools such as standing repo facilities. QE becomes a far out-of-the-money put.",
   "QT is estimated to have raised 10y yields by 125bps in the euro area, 40bps in the US and 110bps in Japan. QT adds about 50bps more to long-end duration until 2033.",
   "Corporate bonds are an imperfect substitute for sovereign duration. Hyperscaler IG issuance is about USD108bn in 2025, USD250bn expected in 2026 and close to USD400bn in 2027, roughly 10-20% of net Treasury supply. Meta's 30-year trades 75bps over Treasuries.",
   "EU Bonds have preserved their convenience yield through recent turmoil and could position Europe as a high-quality long-duration supplier supporting the euro's international role.",
   "The long end is cheap with an extra term premium of 50-100bps on a 30-year bond. Allianz expects a duration revival within 2-5 years from green, infrastructure, defense and ageing needs, which would erase the premium."
  ],

 {
  "source": "Allianz Research",
  "title": "K-shaped construction: AI builds, housing stalls",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-25",
  "insights": [
   "US private data-center construction spending hit USD96.5bn annualized in September, 90% above a year earlier and over ten times 2019. It is 12.2% of private non-residential construction.",
   "Total US construction spending is -2.7% y/y in September but -4.8% excluding data centers. The segment is both the main support of the cycle and a concentration risk. A flattening of data-center spending would push the whole category to -3 to -3.5% a year.",
   "Europe's data-center build is far smaller. FLAP-D hubs have about 1.4 GW under construction against 66-80 GW in the US, and just over 750 MW should be added across Europe in 2026, with power the main constraint.",
   "Three constraints on data centers: labor (79% of North American markets report shortages, over 93% in Europe), power (PJM gas projects deliver 2030-2031), and politics (opposition to a local data center rose from 42% to 75% in one poll).",
   "After the Democratic midterm sweep, Allianz does not expect the cycle to end. Texas and New York pauses could be reinforced, turning a cost constraint into a volume constraint by 2028. About 30 GW of 2028 capacity sits in states where a pause-favoring candidate was running.",
   "2027 data-center volumes look secure, since about three-quarters of the 33.8 GW expected to be delivered is already under construction. Hyperscalers can absorb the costs while smaller developers and projects without secured power are most exposed.",

  "source": "Bank of America",
  "title": "The Oil Gusher: Long-term oil demand: Peak to plateau?",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-25",
  "insights": [
   "BofA sees long-term oil demand peaking around 2030 at about 108mb/d, then declining to under 100mb/d by 2040 and under 90mb/d by 2050, a long plateau rather than a sharp peak.",
   "All base case outlooks except OPEC show roughly flat demand of about 102-106mb/d into 2030. OPEC expects 113mb/d in 2030 and 124.1mb/d in 2050 in its reference case.",
   "OPEC's most bearish scenario sits above every other agency's base case. BofA questions whether this is wishful thinking or an attempt to impose discipline on members seeking to recover market share once Hormuz and new export pipelines allow flows to recover.",
   "TotalEnergies' 2026 Energy Outlook calls Net Zero 2050 beyond reach. Its Trends base case implies 2.5-2.8C of warming by 2100, with oil demand plateauing near current levels into 2030 and falling to 93mb/d by 2050.",
   "The IEA WEO 2026 has five scenarios. STEPS levels off at 103mb/d around 2030, CPS reaches 106mb/d in 2035 and 114mb/d in 2050, ARC falls to 85mb/d by 2050, and NZE falls to 28mb/d. All scenarios exceed 1.5C of warming by 2050.",
   "Road transport is the key driver of demand decline. Under STEPS road oil demand falls about 5% by 2035, while petchem rises 17% and aviation 25%. OPEC instead sees about 6mb/d of road demand growth to 2050.",
   "COP31 draft '35x35' targets electricity at 35% of final energy consumption by 2035, backed by more than 75 countries. The fossil fuel phase-out language and finance-alignment language were dropped or diluted, and methane language was softened.",
   "BofA highlights TTE's Integrated Power portfolio, with FCF breakeven expected in 2026, positive FCF in 2027 and 12% ROACE by 2030. This lowers TTE's oil price breakeven as Brent normalises toward BofA's $60-80/bbl mid-cycle.",
   "Back-solved valuations show European Big Oils discount an average long-term Brent of about $66/bbl. TTE and Galp are lowest at under $45/bbl, with Repsol and OMV at the high end. BofA uses $70/bbl from 2028.",
   "European Big Oils show average organic FCF yield of 15.8% in 2026, falling to 10.7% in 2027 and 9.1% in 2028. Aggregate 2026 organic FCF post distributions is $77bn and FCF surplus is $58bn.",
   "BP has the highest gearing of the group, about 30% on BofA's definition at YE26 versus about 15% for TTE and Shell. Repsol is closest to sub-investment grade on credit ratings.",
   "Consensus has revised 2026 net income up 197% on average versus share prices up 40% YTD. BofA estimates are 2% ahead of consensus on 2026 net income, organic CFFO and EBITDA.",
   "Commodity backdrop: Brent about $92/bbl, TTF about EUR82/MWh, European gas storage 70% full versus 81% a year ago, European refining margin about $24/bbl, and US crude cover about 25 days, below the five-year average.",

  "source": "Cr\u00e9dit Agricole CIB",
  "title": "2027 Treasury supply & debt limit outlook",
  "type": "rates",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-25",
  "insights": [
   "CACIB expects Treasury to hold coupon auction sizes unchanged near term and start raising issuance in H2 2027, mainly in the 2- to 7-year sector, with increases beginning in August 2027.",
   "Gross coupon issuance is forecast to rise modestly to about USD4.5trn in 2027 from USD4.4trn in 2026. Net marketable borrowing is forecast at roughly USD2.1trn in 2027.",
   "Long-end issuance is the key uncertainty. Treasury is weighing investor demand, market functioning and taxpayer cost. TIPS auction sizes are expected to stay broadly unchanged through 2027.",
   "Net bill issuance is estimated at USD800-900bn in 2027 versus about USD721bn in FY2026. Bill supply should fall in December on tax receipts and rise again in January.",
   "Bills are about USD7.4trn, or roughly 23% of marketable debt, below historical peaks. This leaves room to lean on bills, and any signal of a modestly shorter WAM would support longer-dated Treasuries by easing long-end supply.",
   "Bill demand is supported by money market funds with nearly USD8trn in assets (government MMFs about USD6.6trn) and by Fed MBS reinvestment bill purchases of about USD14bn over the next four weeks. The Fed is not doing reserve management bill purchases in the coming four-week period.",
   "Treasury debt is projected to hit the USD41.1trn statutory limit in early 2027, triggering extraordinary measures worth a few hundred USDbn.",
   "The debt limit X-date is likely in Q4 2027, when extraordinary measures and the TGA are exhausted and markets begin pricing default risk.",
   "Ahead of the X-date Treasury should cut bill issuance and draw down the TGA, which lifts bank reserves, and MMFs shift from bills to repo, pushing repo rates lower.",
   "After Congress raises or suspends the limit, Treasury will rebuild the TGA through heavy bill issuance, draining reserves and redirecting MMF flows back to bills."

  "insights": [
   "MS raises 12-month S&P 500 price target to 8,700 (19x forward EPS of $458). Drivers are healthy EPS growth, lower oil, stabilizing rate volatility, AI investment and valuations below fair value.",
   "MS sees the early-cycle to mid-cycle transition (called in July) ending, with a more stable mid-cycle backdrop in 2027. EPS growth stays healthy but its rate of change moderates as operating leverage matures and the Fed normalizes toward less accommodative policy.",

   "EPS forecasts: 2026 $369 (34% growth), 2027 $420 (14%), 2028 $458 (9%). Earnings growth is the primary target driver, with modest multiple expansion from about 18x to 19x. MS fair value is about 19.5x.",
   "Stay with Quality but rotate more cyclically. Industrials is the top sector pick on improving revisions, broadening backlogs and post-correction valuations. Parts of Financials and Consumer Discretionary are attractive, and MS is now overweight Consumer Discretionary.",

   "AI adoption is a high-conviction theme. 44% of S&P 500 companies cited a quantifiable AI benefit versus 32% a year ago, and 26% cited financial impact versus 16%. Adopters show faster NTM EPS growth. AI cost mentions are rising, at about 22% of companies versus 8%.",
   "AI capex remains intact. TMT forecasts keep hyperscaler spend at about $1.6T in 2027 and $1.8T in 2028. MS adds lease capex of about $195B, bringing total 2027 capex to $1.58T. Capex growth moderates from about 100% in 2026 to about 60% in 2027 and about 14% in 2028.",

  "insights": [
   "S&P 500 had its worst week since Liberation Day (April 2025) and the Nasdaq Composite its worst since 2020. Nasdaq is down on the year and in technical bear-market territory after being up 18.7% on October 6. Friday was the S&P's 7th straight decline, the longest streak since February 2020.",
   "Selling has spread well beyond AI and Tech. Weekly S&P decliners outnumbered gainers by more than 15:1, and S&P forward P/E fell to 16.5x while earnings revision breadth stays positive in the US and Europe.",
   "Nvidia beat revenue expectations by about $7B and guided about $5B ahead, yet fell 22.7% on the week. Its forward P/E relative to the S&P is at a record low, with doubts centred on export controls, financing and AI returns.",
   "Consumer prints were mixed. Walmart showed weaker US comps at about 40x forward earnings, Target traffic grew 5%, Ross comps were +8% but below buyside hopes, and WSM fell about 15% despite positive comps. TJX Marmaxx comps +2% vs 1% expected, and MS sees a re-rating case.",
   "Macro signals show a growth scare while activity data stays resilient. The 2Y yield fell 24bps, copper fell 9.9%, WTI fell 5.8%, control-group retail sales beat, claims are low and Indeed postings hit a 19-month high.",
   "The Fed is the central debate. Markets price about 62bps of further hikes over ten months. Tighter financial conditions from lower equities and a stronger dollar add restraint, and QDS says price action mirrors 2018. A change in the expected path could give relief before any formal pivot.",
   "Asia sold off hard on Friday: Taiwan -6.2%, Korea -5.2%, Nikkei -5.1%, with KOSPI below 5,000 and over 300 Taiwan stocks limit-down. Tighter US export controls cut Alibaba FY28-29 revenue and EBITA estimates despite cloud growth guidance of 30-45% in FY28 and 50% in FY29.",
   "Europe had its worst week since Liberation Day, with a flight to defensives. Global Staples now trade at a 73% P/E premium to IT, the largest on record, after outperforming Tech by 49% in under two months, the biggest rotation since March 2001.",
   "New US export controls on advanced AI chips and overseas compute are more restrictive than expected. MS expects slower data center builds in Malaysia and Thailand, with US developers such as EQIX, CIFR, GLXY and RIOT preferred.",
   "Gold is down a third from January highs, its biggest 12M drawdown since the early 1980s, with 14D RSI at a 3-year low. Higher dollar and yields weighed, even as 10Y real yields came off highs.",
   "Hedge fund positioning is de-grossing. US L/S net leverage fell 5ppts to 41% (6th percentile since 2010) and gross fell 4ppts to 195%. Funds are net short Momentum for the first time since April 2025, and nets could drop below 40% after Friday.",
   "MS strategists turned constructive for 2027. Wilson raised the S&P 12M target to 8,700 with EPS of $369/$420/$458 for 2026/27/28 and Industrials as top sector. Tang moved global equities to max Overweight, and Zavolock raised the MSCI Europe YE2027 target to 3,030.",

  "insights": [

   "Domestic demand stays weak. Retail sales growth should improve on base effects as trade-in subsidies roll off (2.1% in 2027F vs 1.2% in 2026F), but underlying household demand stays subdued without broader consumption support including services.",
   "Investment: FAI is forecast to rebound to 2.5% in 2027 from -7.9% in 2026 on a very low base. Manufacturing capacity utilization is at a record low and EU-China trade tensions are broadening, so a manufacturing investment rebound is unlikely.",

   "Policy in 2027 is targeted, not broad. No policy rate or RRR cuts are expected unless exports deteriorate materially, and the deficit stays at 4.0%. Special treasury bonds stay at RMB1.3tn and the LGSB quota edges up to RMB4.5tn from RMB4.4tn.",

 {

  "title": "We see a CRWD/ZS tie-up as possible but not probable",
  "type": "equity_research",
  "priority": "high",
  "published": "2026-11-25",
  "insights": [
   "Credible reports after Friday's close say CRWD is in talks to acquire ZS. A deal would be one of the largest in software history and would exceed Google's $32bn Wiz purchase as the largest cyber acquisition.",
   "DB calls a deal highly possible but less likely than not. The logic is TAM expansion and growth accretion from combining the #1 players in the two control points most critical for securing AI.",
   "Street models ARR exiting Jan 2028 at +24% y/y for CRWD vs +17% for ZS, so the deal would dilute CRWD's organic growth on the surface. DB argues adding ZS would roughly double CRWD's $140bn CY26 TAM via ZT Users, ZT Branch, ZT Cloud and Data Security.",
   "DB sees revenue synergies from combined products, consolidation and distribution outweighing dyssynergies from product overlap or channel conflict. CRWD's Falcon Flex commercial model would be layered onto ZS.",
   "DB fieldwork and guidance implying three consecutive years of 20%+ NNARR growth suggest CRWD would transact from strength. At Black Hat 2026, AI security peers cited CRWD's minimal native network presence as a product gap.",
   "PANW and NTSK may be seen initially as competitive losers. DB suspects ZS was the main donor of PANW's recent next-gen displacements and that ZS inside Falcon would be harder to displace. CRWD's pivot validates network telemetry importance, so DB sees ample network security opportunity despite higher SASE intensity.",
   "Terms are unknown and DB expects a heavy stock component. Any consideration above about $30bn would need equity funding, roughly net 5x DBe PF Adj. EBITDA.",
   "ZS has a $32bn market cap vs a recent high above $43bn less than a month ago and $55bn last year. The average Street PT implies a $40bn market cap, so DB thinks a substantial premium would be required.",
   "Using PANW/CYBR at 17x EV/NTM revenue, growth-adjusted, implies a ~$55bn ZS market cap. Adjusting for the cyber valuation rise since (BUG +27%) implies closer to $70bn, which DB struggles to see making sense.",

  "insights": [
   "CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler before the open on 11/23, valuing Zscaler at about $43.9bn. GS estimates this implies 11.2x EV/NTM Sales, about 47x EV/FCF and a 34% premium to ZS close on 11/20.",
   "Close is expected in CrowdStrike's 2HFY28 (ends 1/31/28). Both boards approved unanimously and Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry would continue to lead the Zscaler business.",
   "GS says scaled security platforms have mostly used tuck-in deals to outsource R&D. CRWD's comments and PANW's at the CyberArk deal show rising importance of scale and combining network, identity and endpoint telemetry.",
   "CrowdStrike's stated rationale includes entering network security (largest cyber segment, $37bn in 2026E per Gartner), adding Zscaler's Zero Trust SASE, Security for AI and Data Protection to Falcon, and combining datasets to train SafeMind.",
   "CRWD expects cross-sell into 8,000 Zscaler customers that are not yet CrowdStrike customers, with revenue synergies building over 30 months post close to about $1bn annualized run-rate (about 25% of ZS FY27E revenue).",
   "GS views the earnings from CRWD, ZS, PANW and NET as a signal that cyber demand is inflecting, de-risking CY27 outlooks. GS is less concerned than about 2 months ago about an air pocket into 2027.",
   "CRWD 3QF27 net new ARR was $419mn vs Street $347mn (21% above). Revenue was about 4% above, gross margin about 90bps above and EBIT margin about 100bps above, with billings +26%.",
   "CRWD 4Q revenue/ARR guidance is about 1% above Street organically, and FY28 NNARR growth is still expected at least 20% excluding Zscaler. Flex ARR is +100% yoy, Guardian ARR more than doubled qoq to over $100mn, and cloud ARR exceeds $1bn.",
   "ZS 1QF27 net new ARR was $111mn vs Street $96mn (18% above). Revenue beat was only about 1% (smallest in 14 quarters), while NNARR growth ex Red Canary accelerated to 22%.",
